artifacts.summary: Designs and validates a minimal extension to lint-state-writer-boundary.sh for the Python/json.dump channel (zero new live false positives, measured), and decides -- with evidence from the originating incident log -- that a companion write-time Bash PreToolUse hook is also warranted since the actual incident never existed as a scannable file.

memory_candidates.content: When deciding whether a write-time PreToolUse hook should trigger on Bash vs. Write|Edit, match the matcher to where the hazard's bytes actually originate: a live interpreter/shell invocation (e.g. `python3 -c "..."` run via the Bash tool) needs a Bash-command-string hook mirroring guard-destructive-git.sh (reads tool_input.command); authored file content needs a Write|Edit hook mirroring validate-no-task-references.sh (Edit requires reconstructing old_string/new_string against the on-disk file). A content lint scanning only committed files in a source tree cannot catch an ad hoc, uncommitted interpreter invocation regardless of how good its regex is -- verify which shape the actual incident took before assuming a content lint is sufficient.

For a line-oriented regex content lint guarding against a specific Python file-write shape (open(...) targeting a sensitive path), key detection on the write-capable open() call itself -- the path literal plus a write-capable mode token (w/a/r+/w+/a+/x) on the same line -- rather than on a bare json.dump/json.dumps/json.load token. Keying on the json function name alone over-matches every legitimate JSON writer in a codebase (producing a large false-positive/allowlist burden); keying on the open()-call-plus-target-literal-plus-mode naturally covers both the inline `json.dump(obj, open(path,'w'))` shape and the `with open(path,'w') as f:` idiom's own line, generalizes to any path suffix (archive/vault-root variants) for free, and measurably produces zero false positives against an existing large codebase's legitimate Python JSON writers.
